Vikram —

Appreciate the questions. Attached is a short summary and an SOW draft (AurumTech_SOW_v2.pdf) — high level answers below. I pulled in Sean on pricing and Hannah for SLA/operational constraints.

Summary (quick table):
- 12-month: baseline reserved pool = 24 A100-equivalent GPUs; standard discount = 10% off list hosted/Dedicated unit pricing; start window = 8–12 weeks from signed SOW. No free staging buffer; burst credits available for a fee.
- 24-month: baseline = 32 A100-equivalent GPUs; discount = 18%; start window = 6–10 weeks; includes a 60-day staging buffer equal to 15% additional capacity (billed at discounted rate).
- 36-month: baseline = 40 A100-equivalent GPUs; discount = 25%; start window = 4–8 weeks; includes a 90-day staging buffer equal to 20% additional capacity and an accelerated capacity-onboarding SLA (priority provisioning).

Throughput & SLOs: baseline throughput targets assume mixed generation workload: ~2,500 concurrent request capacity ~ avg 1,800 tokens/sec sustained aggregate with 99th percentile tail latency target < 500ms for short prompts (<256 tokens). We can carve guaranteed throughput lanes if needed; add-on pricing applies.

Staging buffer explanation: the staging buffer is reserved burst capacity available for short-term traffic spikes during ramp. It is pre-reserved from our pool for your tenant for the staging window; usage is metered and billed at the discounted rate in the SOW. The buffer does not count toward the committed baseline after the staging window ends.

Start date: If signed by Feb 1 and paper completed same week, earliest practical availability for the baseline pool is Mar 10 (6 weeks) for 24-month and Mar 24 (8 weeks) for 12-month. For 36-month we can prioritize and target Mar 3 (4 weeks) with the accelerated SLA.

See attached spreadsheet for line-item pricing and a sample ramp schedule. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through tradeoffs.

Best,
So - Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: AurumTech_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW draft)

- For 24-month, is product willing to reduce start window to 5 weeks if we accept a 20% staging buffer (instead of 15%) for first 30 days at no extra charge? Operationally — Hannah, can we guarantee priority provisioning to meet a 5-week target for 24-month if we accept that concession?
